content.title: Phishing Simulation Debrief: Invoice and Payment-Redirect Fraud
content.summary: Learn how to spot and report fraudulent vendor payment-redirect requests targeting Finance workflows.
content.body_markdown:
## Oops! That was a security simulation

We all get tricked sometimes. Last month we covered general phishing awareness; this time we are focusing on invoice and payment-redirect fraud targeting accounts payable [S1], [S6].

### What is happening
Attackers frequently target business payment workflows and vendor payout systems [S6], [S7]. They send emails posing as trusted partners to request sudden changes to bank details or push unexpected invoices [S1], [S4]. These unauthorized alterations can misdirect thousands of dollars to fraudulent accounts [S1].

### How to spot it
- **Sudden payment changes:** Watch for unexpected requests to alter vendor bank account records [S1], [S6].
- **Urgent pressure:** Be cautious of emails creating immediate urgency to bypass standard approval checks [S8].
- **Unrecognized invoices:** Look out for unexpected invoices demanding quick payment [S4].
- **Spoofed addresses:** Check sender email addresses closely for small misspellings or unexpected domains [S1], [S8].

### What to do
- Independently verify all vendor banking change requests using an established phone number before updating details [S1], [S6].
- Strictly follow internal dual-authorization and reconciliation steps for payments [S6].
- Do not click links or open unexpected billing attachments from unverified senders [S4], [S8].

### How to report
If you receive a suspicious payment request or invoice, forward it immediately to security@nebulon.example.com.
key_points: Attackers attempt to alter vendor payment records and misdirect payouts to fake accounts [S1], [S6].
Always verify banking detail updates using trusted out-of-band communication channels [S1], [S6].
Urgent language and unexpected invoice changes are key indicators of billing fraud [S4], [S8].
red_flags: Request to change vendor payment details received unexpectedly via email [S1], [S6].
High-pressure tone warning of service interruption if payment is delayed [S8].
Links pointing to unverified external domains like example.com [S8].
actions: Verify vendor detail changes out-of-band via a confirmed, official phone number before updating records [S1], [S6].
Follow standard accounts payable approval and reconciliation steps [S6].
Report suspicious emails directly to security@nebulon.example.com.
content.report_how: Forward any suspicious email or payment request to security@nebulon.example.com.

phishing_sim.subject: URGENT: Updated Bank Account Details for Pending Vendor Invoices
phishing_sim.body:
Dear Finance Team,

Please note that our bank account details have been updated effective immediately. Please update our vendor profile and direct all future invoice payments to the new account specified at http://www.vendor-billing.example.com/update to avoid service disruption.

Thank you,
Vendor Accounts Payable Team
red_flags: Unsolicited request to change vendor bank payout details [S1], [S6].
Urgent threat of service disruption to force fast action [S8].
Direction to click an external link to update banking credentials [S4], [S8].

CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud

The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a six year old Florida business that claimed to use "advanced cryptographic tools" to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.
